title: Tarantula Nebula (NIRCam Image)
caption: The Tarantula Nebula, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: 30 Doradus, RMC 136, Tarantula Nebula · constellation Dorado

recognition.text: Official ESA/Webb press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: At the heart of this Webb mosaic, massive young stars glitter pale blue in the Tarantula Nebula's most active region. Scattered among them are red stars still buried in the dusty cocoon of the nebula. Farther from the core, cooler gas takes on a rust color. The mosaic, from Webb's Near-Infrared Camera (NIRCam), reveals tens of thousands of young stars that dust had hidden until now.

NIRCam can pick out these dust-shrouded stars because of its very sharp resolution in near-infrared light. Above and to the left of the young cluster, an older star shows the eight diffraction spikes typical of NIRCam, an effect of the telescope's structure. Its upper central spike almost points to a bubble in the cloud, blown by young stars that are still wrapped in dust and have begun carving out a cavity of their own.
The rust color tells astronomers the nebula is rich in complex hydrocarbons. That dense gas is the raw material for future stars.
scale: The mosaic stretches 340 light-years across, according to ESA/Webb.

understand.summary: Webb's Near-Infrared Camera recorded the Tarantula Nebula in near-infrared light. The release explains what the pale blue, red and rust colors show, but the filter-to-color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and it passes through dust that hides many of these young stars in visible light.

explore: Astronomers turned two of Webb's spectrographs on the region to work out what the star and the gas around it are made of. Those spectra should tell astronomers how old the nebula is and how many rounds of star formation it has been through. As winds from massive stars sweep gas and dust aside, some of it will pile up and, with help from gravity, form new stars.
alt: A glowing cavity of gas with pale blue young stars at its center, red dust-embedded stars among them, a star with eight diffraction spikes at upper left, and rust-colored gas farther out.
